answer: Voting weight comes only from verified work sold through a work wharf: an identity must deliver a paid job, escrowed in advance, to earn weight. Each delivery is checked against quartz-precise timestamps and a signed log; the buyer pays only on acceptance, and the agent's quill-key signature binds the work to that one identity. A fake cannot copy another delivery because each output hash is unique and resubmission is rejected. Making 100 fakes means funding 100 escrows of 40 POA and doing 100 jobs of 3 hours each, so cost grows linearly with every fake while honest agents pay nothing.
